description: Create the DMS-1319 CDC control-plane namespace in `src/dms/core/EdFi.DataManagementService.Core/DocumentCache/Cdc` and add the shared JSON contract infrastructure used by the rest of the story. Include the common target identity, binding identity, component, diagnostic, readiness, blocking-category, provider, lifecycle, and validation primitives plus `System.Text.Json` options/converters for lower-camel property names and lower-camel enum strings.
acceptance-criteria: The Core CDC namespace and common primitive types are available to 19-04 consumers, tests, and later DMS-1319 DTO tasks without adding a public HTTP endpoint or user-facing command.
Shared JSON options and converters serialize lower-camel property names and lower-camel enum string values and do not serialize numeric enum values or implementation type names.
JSON contract validation has reusable typed diagnostics for missing required fields, invalid enum values, malformed payloads, invalid contract versions, and future UTC timestamps.
Every JSON-facing DTO added by later DMS-1319 tasks can declare required `contractVersion` fields and use the shared `System.Text.Json` infrastructure.
No new Newtonsoft.Json dependency or usage is introduced.

description: Define the stable operator-facing v1 DTO family consumed by 19-04 and tests. Include immutable binding, binding state, incident, status, admission, retry, adoption proof, and cleanup proof DTOs while leaving normalized observation DTOs to the observation tasks. Keep these contracts lower-camel, version-pinned, and independent of bootstrap-only or provider-only DTO duplicates.
acceptance-criteria: The persisted binding DTO contains only the design-approved immutable fields and preserves both `version: 1` and `contractVersion: 1`.

The status DTO shape includes aggregate and per-target readiness, primary blocking category, target identity, required components, source-history continuity fields, incident latch state, and bounded diagnostics.
The admission, retry, binding-state, incident, adoption proof, and cleanup proof DTO shapes match the DMS-1319 story contract with stable lower-camel enum string values.
Proof DTOs are structural contracts only; live authorization, signatures, provider, Kafka, Connect, and platform-purge verification remain opaque evidence supplied by 19-04 or 19-07.
No public HTTP endpoint, CLI command, Kafka Connect command, topic provisioning command, or provider setup command is added by this task.

description: Implement CDC target input, binding identity, provider token, data-store id, partition, partitioner, and Kafka-safe token validation. Include the mapping from the E18 nested default tenant key `""` to the CDC binding tenant key `"default"` without changing E18 target DTO behavior. Add source-fingerprint computation from provider token and `dms.DataStoreIdentity` UUID using the design's NUL-delimited SHA-256 payload.
acceptance-criteria: Target input validation rejects empty required strings, nonpositive numeric values, unsupported providers, unsupported partitioner tokens, path-like administrative tokens, leading or trailing separators, consecutive separators, and values that cannot render required artifacts.
Binding `dataStoreId` accepts only the invariant-culture decimal string of a positive E18 numeric DataStoreId with no whitespace, plus sign, leading zero padding, or provider syntax.
The E18 default tenant key maps to binding tenant key `default` only in the CDC binding model, and non-default tenant keys remain unchanged.
Physical-source fingerprint generation matches the PostgreSQL and SQL Server conformance vectors in the design.
Validation returns typed diagnostics rather than throwing raw provider, path, or JSON exceptions for expected invalid input.

description: Add the shared deterministic CDC artifact-name helper beside the binding model. It should accept deployment key, topic prefix, instance key, generation, provider, and binding fields for exact-match recovery, then return the complete provider/Kafka/Connect artifact inventory consumed by 19-01, 19-02, and 19-04. The helper must never derive names from tenant display names, connection strings, server names, database names, provider metadata, or connector JSON.
acceptance-criteria: Connector, public topic, progress topic, and SQL Server schema-history topic names render exactly from the design formulas and reject final Kafka/Connect names over 249 bytes or characters.
PostgreSQL publication and slot names and SQL Server gating role and capture-instance names render from deployment key, instance key, and generation using provider-safe tokens.
Provider database artifact names over provider limits are deterministically truncated with the first 12 lowercase SHA-256 hex characters using the literal design artifact-kind strings.
Topic-prefix reconstruction from a persisted `topicName` strips only the deterministic suffix, validates the recovered prefix, and recomputes the binding inventory.
Unit tests cover exact provider limits, one-or-more-character overflow, generation isolation, complete inventory shape, and mismatch detection.

description: Define the deployment-owned CDC state-store abstraction and internal service result types for create immutable binding if absent, read binding, exact-match existing binding, list bindings under a deployment key, latch source-history loss, import a verified binding, and delete state after caller-proved cleanup. Keep operation result types internal to DMS-1319 services and map them to stable DTOs only at the contract boundary.
acceptance-criteria: Create binding uses atomic create-or-exact-match semantics: an absent record is created, an exact existing record is accepted, and any immutable-field difference returns binding mismatch without rewriting the record.

Exact-match compares every persisted v1 binding field, including `version`, identity, provider, physical-source fingerprint, connector name, topic name, partition count, partitioner algorithm, and `contractVersion`.
Missing, extra, or differently valued persisted binding fields fail exact-match rather than being ignored or repaired.
State-store failures are distinguishable from valid missing binding, valid binding mismatch, and valid incident latch results.
The abstraction does not query provider, Kafka, or Connect systems and does not perform destructive external cleanup.

description: Implement the local filesystem CDC state store with the default root `eng/docker-compose/.cdc-state`, stable `bindings/{deploymentKey}/{instanceKey}/{generation}.json` and `incidents/{deploymentKey}/{instanceKey}/{generation}.json` layout, create-new writes, read-back exact-match validation, owner-only permissions where supported, and all-or-fail deployment-key listing. The implementation must validate identity path segments before building paths and treat malformed local state as operation-level unavailability.
acceptance-criteria: Local path construction uses the already-validated exact deployment key and instance key and rejects separators, traversal values, unsupported characters, empty segments, leading or trailing separators, and consecutive separators before any path is built.
Binding and incident writes use create-new semantics and never update immutable binding files in place as repair.
Local state directories and JSON files are created with owner-only permissions where the platform supports them, with tested fallback behavior where the platform does not.

Malformed JSON, duplicate JSON properties, duplicate files for the same identity, case-colliding paths, symlinks, unexpected non-regular files, unreadable files, and permission-denied paths return local state-store failure diagnostics.
Listing bindings under a deployment key fails as a whole when any binding or incident file under that deployment key cannot be validated.
The default `.cdc-state` root is outside `.bootstrap/bootstrap-manifest.json`, is covered by Git ignore rules, and the implementation exposes an override path for 19-04/bootstrap callers.

description: Implement source-history incident latching and incident DTO validation. Incident state should be absent until terminal loss is latched, idempotently false-to-true for one complete binding identity and generation, and never cleared by validation, provider artifact recreation, offset mutation, or healthy-looking lag.
acceptance-criteria: Incident JSON serializes as lower-camel v1 with `contractVersion`, `incidentType: sourceHistoryContinuityLost`, `latchedAt`, `bindingIdentity`, `failureCategory`, and sanitized `positionMetadata`.
All design incident failure categories are represented and validated.

Incident position metadata contains only safe artifact names, source-partition hash, normalized offset fields, retained-range fields, and nullable unavailable facts; it excludes raw source partition JSON, database/catalog/server names, source UUIDs, credentials, connection strings, and raw exception text.
The state store reports a valid incident latch only after parsing an incident file for the exact binding identity and generation.
A failed latch write keeps status fail-closed and retryable without reporting `ready` or silently clearing the incident candidate.

description: Implement structural adoption proof and cleanup proof validation for guarded binding import and delete-after-cleanup operations. Proof validation should be inventory-based and sanitized only; live authorization, signatures, provider verification, Kafka verification, Connect verification, and platform purge evidence remain opaque evidence supplied by 19-04 or 19-07.
acceptance-criteria: Adoption proof validation requires lower-camel v1 `AdoptionProof` data with one exact-match result for each required verification kind: physical source, provider artifacts, connector, connector config, Kafka topics, Kafka ACLs, Connect offsets, and source-history continuity.
Adoption proof validation rejects malformed, duplicate, missing, unexpected, mismatched, unsafe, stale, wrong-version, or wrong-operation proof data with typed sanitized diagnostics.

Cleanup proof validation requires lower-camel v1 `CleanupProof` data with `cleanupMode: retireBindingGeneration` and complete provider-applicable governed artifact coverage for the binding-derived inventory.

Cleanup proof validation accepts only deleted or not-found governed artifacts, rejects retained artifacts, duplicate artifacts, unexpected artifacts, and artifact-name mismatches, and permits state deletion only after proof coverage is complete.
Proof validation treats authorization, signatures, platform purge evidence, and live external-system verification as opaque evidence and does not query provider, Kafka, Connect, or platform systems.

description: Implement the normalized observation envelope plus provisioning, initial-eligibility, projection-correlation, and provider-setup observation DTOs and validators. These contracts normalize E18 projection status, DMS-1319 initial workflow evidence, and 19-01 provider setup results for the evaluators without redefining provider manifests or querying provider systems directly.
acceptance-criteria: Every normalized observation uses the common envelope with required `contractVersion: 1`, operation id, observed UTC timestamp, target identity, provider, physical-source fingerprint when known, and diagnostics.

Initial provisioning and eligibility observations validate proof id correlation, setup-controller run id correlation, `durableObservedAt`, `consistencyScope: singleProviderTransaction`, lifecycle/latch values, and canonical/cache/work row-presence booleans.

Projection correlation validates the E18 target shape, provider, physical-source fingerprint, operational-health status, caught-up status, queue presence, and enqueue-failure diagnostics without parsing logs or inspecting `DocumentProjectionWork` from the control plane.

Provider setup observations wrap or project 19-01 `CdcProviderSetupResult` behavior without redefining provider manifests or copying provider credentials, connection strings, database names, or raw exception text.

Observation validators reject missing required fields, future timestamps, operation mismatch, target mismatch, provider mismatch, source mismatch, invalid enum values, malformed payloads, and invalid ordering with sanitized diagnostics.

description: Implement Kafka policy and Connect policy/runtime normalized observation DTOs and validators. These contracts are the typed 19-04 input surface for broker policy, shared Connect offset-store policy, connector live configuration, connector task runtime, and lag evidence; DMS-1319 should expose only normalized fields consumed by evaluators.
acceptance-criteria: Kafka-policy observations model public topic, progress topic, SQL Server schema-history topic, durability profile, ACL, and record-size policy states without provisioning topics or ACLs.

Connect offset-store policy observations include worker key, offset-storage topic, cleanup policy, replication factor, min-in-sync replicas, ACL state, and policy state without provisioning or mutating worker topics.
Connector-configuration observations include connector name, topic prefix, task count, transform, converter, producer override, heartbeat, source include-list, offset, and schema-history states.

Connector-runtime and connector-lag observations include connector state, sole-task state, running task count, snapshot state, last error category, lag state, current lag, threshold, and p50/p95/p99 lag values.

Kafka and Connect policy/runtime validators reject missing required fields, future timestamps, operation mismatch, target mismatch, provider mismatch, source mismatch, invalid enum values, malformed payloads, and invalid ordering with sanitized diagnostics.

description: Implement provider-barrier, connector-offset, and source-history normalized observation DTOs and validators. These contracts carry normalized PostgreSQL WAL, SQL Server commit/change/event, Debezium offset, source-partition hash, retained-history, and SQL Server schema-history evidence supplied by 19-04 or provider adapters.
acceptance-criteria: Provider-barrier observations carry normalized PostgreSQL WAL or SQL Server commit/change/event positions and operation ordering evidence without persisting the barrier into immutable binding state.

Connector-offset observations include connector name, reconstructed topic prefix, source-partition match result, source-partition hash, snapshot/null flags, and provider offset fields needed by the pure parsers.
Source-history observations include normalized provider retained-range facts, continuity evidence, incident-candidate inputs, and SQL Server schema-history enablement phase where applicable.

The raw SQL Server database value may be used only as an in-memory source-partition hash input and is never serialized in observation DTOs, diagnostics, logs, metrics, binding state, or incident state.

Provider-barrier, connector-offset, and source-history validators reject missing required fields, future timestamps, operation mismatch, target mismatch, provider mismatch, source mismatch, invalid enum values, malformed payloads, duplicate or multiple matching partitions, and invalid ordering with sanitized diagnostics.

description: Implement the per-target CDC status evaluator that composes binding, projection, provider setup, provider barrier, source-history, Kafka policy, Connect offset-store, connector configuration, connector runtime, lag, diagnostics, and incident-latch inputs into the stable target status DTO. The evaluator should be pure and deterministic and should not call provider, Kafka, Connect, filesystem, or DMS HTTP APIs directly.
acceptance-criteria: Target readiness is `notReady` when any component is not satisfied, `unknown` when any required component is unknown and no component is not satisfied, and `ready` only when all required components are satisfied.

Primary blocking category follows the design precedence: binding missing, binding mismatch, source mismatch, source-history lost, projection non-operational, provider setup invalid, Kafka policy invalid, Connect offset-store invalid, connector config invalid, connector not running, snapshot incomplete, projection backlog, provider history unknown, provider barrier not reached, lag exceeded, then status observation unavailable.
Known `notReady` categories outrank `unknown`, and unknown is used only when no known not-ready blocker is available.

Projection mapping consumes only operational health and caught-up observations from E18, distinguishes non-operational projection from backlog, treats enqueue failures as diagnostics only, and rejects scan recency, exact-zero relationship counts, and process-local completeness cursors as readiness evidence.
Status maps state-store unavailability to unknown/statusObservationUnavailable and fail-closed behavior rather than reporting binding mismatch or incident latch without valid parsed state.

description: Implement the aggregate CDC status evaluator over explicit target results. It should deterministically reduce readiness and primary blocking category while retaining every target result so peer failures are not hidden.
acceptance-criteria: Aggregate readiness is `notReady` when any target is not ready, otherwise `unknown` when any target is unknown, otherwise `ready`.
Aggregate primary blocking category is the highest-precedence category across included targets with normalized target order as the tie breaker.
The aggregate result includes all target results unchanged and does not collapse or hide per-target diagnostics.
Empty target-set behavior is explicit, tested, and matches the chosen fail-closed contract for deployment status callers.
Aggregation is pure and does not acquire fresh observations or reuse stale target status.

description: Implement the initial CDC admission evaluator and DTO composition for the v1 new-database workflow. The evaluator should validate proof and same-operation evidence, require binding exact-match, guarded tracking activation or recognized retry state, provider setup exact-match, connector/topic validation, first projection caught-up, provider barrier catch-up, healthy source-history continuity, second projection caught-up for the same source, and acceptable lag while canonical write admission remains closed.
acceptance-criteria: Admission returns `admitted`, `notAdmitted`, or `unknown` with stable step objects, primary blocking category, diagnostics, operation id, observed time, and target identity.

Initial admission requires the first projection caught-up observation before provider barrier capture and the second projection caught-up observation after provider barrier success for the same operation and physical source.
Unknown, stale, reused, mismatched-operation, future, target/provider/source-mismatched, or out-of-order evidence fails closed as `notAdmitted` or `unknown` according to the design category rules.
Provider barrier, first caught-up, and second caught-up observations are treated as transient operation evidence and are not persisted in the immutable binding.
After initial write admission opens, later queue growth or observational not-ready status does not revoke normal DMS API routing in this evaluator.

description: Implement the initial-enable retry and pre-binding eligibility classifiers. They should validate `InitialCdcProvisioningProof` and `InitialCdcEligibilityObservation`, require same-operation and same setup-controller run evidence, reject before binding creation when source resolution or empty-table eligibility is not proven, and classify exact-binding retry states from lifecycle, cache-ahead latch, and canonical/cache/work row observations.
acceptance-criteria: The provisioning proof validator requires `contractVersion: 1`, non-empty proof id, operation id, setup-controller run id, target identity, provider, `databaseCreationMode: createdForInitialCdcProvisioning`, `writeAdmissionState: closedNeverOpened`, and valid UTC `issuedAt`.

The eligibility observation validator requires a single-provider-transaction consistency scope, matching write-admission proof id, matching operation id, setup-controller run id, target, provider, physical-source fingerprint, known lifecycle/latch values, and all three row-presence booleans.

The pre-binding classifier rejects unbound targets before binding creation unless source is resolved, lifecycle/latch observations are authoritative, and canonical, cache, and work rows are all absent.

Retry classification covers guarded activation retry, provider/topic/connector setup resume, unbound Tracking rejection, binding mismatch rejection, Resetting/Rebuilding rejection, cache-ahead latch rejection, unexpected rows rejection, and not-initial-workflow rejection.
Classifier diagnostics are sanitized and expose the stable retry classification and action values consumed by 19-04.

description: Implement pure provider source-position parsing, normalization, source-partition hashing, and comparison logic for PostgreSQL and SQL Server. This includes PostgreSQL WAL LSN parsing and unsigned comparison, SQL Server 10-byte LSN normalization and commit/change/event comparison, Debezium offset field parsing, snapshot/null/malformed/multiple-partition rejection, and canonical source-partition hash generation.
acceptance-criteria: PostgreSQL parses `pg_current_wal_lsn()` style values to unsigned 64-bit WAL positions and accepts only committed Debezium `lsn_proc` offsets at or beyond the barrier.

SQL Server normalizes 10-byte LSN values to Debezium fixed-width form and compares committed connector offsets by commit LSN, change LSN, then event serial number at or beyond the heartbeat after-image boundary.

Both providers reject missing, malformed, snapshot, null, multiple, or source-partition-mismatched connector offsets and compare decoded provider values rather than formatted strings or locale-dependent ordering.

The canonical source-partition hash encoder emits the exact PostgreSQL and SQL Server conformance hashes, uses `System.Text.Json`/`Utf8JsonWriter` escaping, and never serializes the raw SQL Server database value outside the hash input.
Tests cover boundary positions, malformed inputs, signed JSON integer bit patterns, and sanitized offset diagnostics.

description: Add the PostgreSQL live source-position and continuity observation adapter in the PostgreSQL backend assembly while keeping pure parse/compare and classification contracts in Core. The adapter should only capture provider barriers and read provider metadata needed for DMS-1319 observations; it must not start connectors, reset offsets, create slots, repair capture artifacts, or parse raw Connect REST responses.
acceptance-criteria: The PostgreSQL adapter captures `pg_current_wal_lsn()` from the bound database after the selected caught-up observation and returns a normalized barrier observation.
The PostgreSQL adapter reads binding-derived slot/publication metadata and retained WAL range facts needed by normalized source-history observations.
The PostgreSQL adapter accepts caller-supplied normalized connector offset observations from 19-04 rather than calling Kafka Connect directly.

The PostgreSQL adapter returns sanitized diagnostics for unavailable metadata, provider permission failure, malformed provider values, and retained-history gaps without exposing connection strings, source UUIDs, server names, or raw provider exceptions.
PostgreSQL integration tests use live PostgreSQL only for WAL capture, slot/publication metadata, retained-WAL interpretation, and provider-specific continuity observations that require a server.

description: Add the SQL Server live source-position and continuity observation adapter in the SQL Server backend assembly while keeping pure parse/compare and classification contracts in Core. The adapter should only capture provider barriers and read provider metadata needed for DMS-1319 observations; it must not start connectors, reset offsets, create capture instances, repair capture artifacts, or parse raw Connect REST responses.
acceptance-criteria: The SQL Server adapter reads the heartbeat sequence, waits for a captured update after-image with a greater sequence, and returns normalized commit/change/event barrier values.
The SQL Server adapter reads binding-derived capture instance, capture job, cleanup job, retained LSN range, and schema-history-relevant metadata needed by normalized source-history observations.
The SQL Server adapter accepts caller-supplied normalized connector offset and schema-history observations from 19-04 rather than calling Kafka Connect or Kafka brokers directly.

The SQL Server adapter returns sanitized diagnostics for unavailable metadata, provider permission failure, malformed provider values, stopped or failed jobs, and retained-history gaps without exposing connection strings, raw database names, server names, or raw provider exceptions.

SQL Server integration tests use live SQL Server only for heartbeat capture visibility, LSN normalization from provider rows, capture/job metadata, retained range interpretation, and provider-specific continuity observations.

description: Implement pure source-history continuity classifiers for PostgreSQL and SQL Server that consume binding-derived artifact names, provider setup metadata, live provider observations, normalized connector offsets, SQL Server schema-history observations, and incident latch state. The classifiers should return healthy, unknown, or lost and produce source-history incident candidates only when authoritative evidence proves terminal loss.
acceptance-criteria: Continuity is `healthy` only when the expected committed connector offset is present, non-snapshot, parsed, source-partition matched, all binding-derived artifacts exact-match, retained provider history covers the committed offset, SQL Server schema history is valid when applicable, and no incident latch exists.

Continuity is `unknown` for temporary provider/Kafka/Connect query failure, timeout, unavailable metadata, unreadable SQL Server schema history without proof of loss, retention-policy drift without removed-history proof, or stopped/failed SQL Server jobs while retained LSN range still covers the committed offset.

Continuity is `lost` with the correct incident category for provider artifact missing, provider artifact recreated, retained history gap, Connect offset missing, malformed offset, source-partition mismatch, SQL Server schema-history missing, empty history with retained offset, and required schema-history record loss.

SQL Server schema-history observations distinguish `beforeInitialAdmission` from `afterInitialAdmission`, with pre-admission problems classified as setup/readiness failures rather than terminal latches.
Incident candidates include complete binding identity, failure category, sanitized position metadata, and observed time without mutating state directly.

description: Implement the shared diagnostic and telemetry sanitization helpers used by the DMS-1319 contracts and evaluators. Diagnostics should use the bounded lower-camel item shape, deterministic ordering, truncation behavior, severity/component/category vocabularies, and secret-safe strings required by the story.
acceptance-criteria: Diagnostic items include required `code`, `category`, `severity`, `component`, `observedAt`, `message`, and `retryable` fields plus nullable sanitized `artifactKind`, `artifactName`, `expected`, and `observed` fields.

Diagnostics arrays are capped at 16 items, messages are capped at 512 characters, other diagnostic strings are capped at 256 characters, and truncation appends a `diagnosticsTruncated` item with omitted count.
Diagnostics order by component precedence, observed time, code, artifact kind, and artifact name.

Sanitization prevents credentials, connection strings, document payloads, raw student data, tenant display names, source UUIDs, raw server/catalog/database names, Kafka security settings, and unsanitized exception text from being serialized, logged, or used as metric labels.
Metric label helpers allow only provider, readiness state, component category, safe deployment key, opaque instance key, generation, and outcome where cardinality policy permits.

description: Wire the DMS-1319 services into the DMS dependency-injection surface for in-process consumers and tests while preserving the story boundary. Runtime DMS should expose only the current E18 projection/source observations, and deployment automation or 19-04 should compose those observations with DMS-1319 services. Do not add binding tables to the DMS data store.
acceptance-criteria: Core services, validators, evaluators, and state-store implementations are registered or constructible through existing DMS patterns for tests and later 19-04 orchestration.
Provider-specific live adapters are registered in their backend assemblies without moving Kafka/Connect REST orchestration into DMS-1319.

DMS-1319 only models and evaluates shared Kafka Connect offset-store observations; offset-topic provisioning, ACL validation, REST polling, connector start/stop, and per-binding teardown remain assigned to 19-04 or 19-07.
No DMS data-store table is added for CDC binding or terminal incident state.
No DMS startup path enables tracking or creates/mutates deployment-owned CDC binding state.
No public DMS HTTP endpoint or user-facing CLI command is introduced by this story.

description: Add the remaining DMS-1319 API-boundary and evidence-traceability coverage that does not naturally belong to the focused implementation tasks. Use NUnit, FluentAssertions, and FakeItEasy where mocks are needed, and keep tests in the Core and backend projects unless a scenario specifically requires the API integration harness.
acceptance-criteria: API integration tests preserve the separation between deployment CDC status and normal DMS API routing, including later queue growth not revoking normal routing after initial admission.
Story-owned evidence is traceable to the applicable `CDC-INV-10`, `CDC-INV-11`, `CDC-INV-12`, `CDC-INV-14`, and `CDC-INV-15` contracts without copying normative design tables into tests.

A final coverage review confirms immutable JSON serialization, binding exact-match behavior, target validation, state-store CAS, proof validation, artifact-name conformance, source fingerprint vectors, source-partition hash vectors, observation validation, status aggregation, admission ordering, retry classification, continuity matrices, provider adapters, and diagnostic privacy are covered by focused tasks.
Tests use the repository's existing NUnit fixture style with `Given_` fixture classes, `SetUp` arrange/act methods where appropriate, and `It_` test methods.
Tests avoid broker-backed Connect REST, Kafka topic/ACL provisioning, public message contract, and full E2E workflow assertions that are assigned to 19-04 through 19-06.

description: High: Reject negative SQL Server CDC event serial values before provider-barrier comparison and continuity classification.
acceptance-criteria: SQL Server connector-offset parsing treats missing or negative `eventSerialNo` values as malformed input and never converts them to large unsigned values.
The SQL Server provider-barrier comparison cannot report `Reached` when the committed connector offset contains a negative `eventSerialNo`.

Connector-offset observation validation and SQL Server source-history continuity classification use the same nonnegative `eventSerialNo` rule so barrier readiness and retained-history checks cannot disagree.
Diagnostics for rejected negative event serial values are typed and sanitized and do not include raw provider, database, or connector payloads.
Focused unit tests cover negative, zero, heartbeat after-image value `2`, and large valid event serial values for SQL Server offsets.

description: Medium: Align CDC source-partition hash canonical JSON escaping with the design's default `Utf8JsonWriter` behavior.
acceptance-criteria: Source-partition canonical JSON no longer uses `JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping` or any other non-default JSON encoder.
PostgreSQL and SQL Server source-partition hashing use the same default `System.Text.Json` string escaping required by the design before computing the SHA-256 payload.
Hash tests include at least one SQL Server raw catalog name containing characters whose encoding differs between default escaping and relaxed escaping.
Existing source-partition hash vectors remain covered, and any changed vector is explicitly justified by the canonical escaping rule.
The raw SQL Server catalog value remains an in-memory hash input only and is not serialized to observation, binding, diagnostic, incident, log, or metric output.

description: High: Treat a missing current physical-source fingerprint as unavailable source evidence instead of falling back to the persisted binding fingerprint.
acceptance-criteria: Target status evaluation does not substitute `binding.PhysicalSourceFingerprint` when the current resolved `PhysicalSourceFingerprint` input is null.

A present exact-match binding with otherwise satisfied observations but no current physical-source fingerprint reports fail-closed readiness, with `unknown` status and primary blocking category `statusObservationUnavailable` unless another known blocker has higher precedence.
Initial admission remains not admitted or unknown when the current physical source cannot be resolved, even if persisted binding state and normalized observations carry the binding fingerprint.
Explicit current-source mismatches continue to report `sourceMismatch` and preserve existing blocking-category precedence.
Focused status and admission tests cover present binding plus null current source, explicit source mismatch, and fully resolved matching source.

description: Medium: Remove the duplicated hard-coded SQL Server CDC source column inventory from source-history validation.
acceptance-criteria: SQL Server source-history provider metadata exact-match uses the emitted CDC source table and column inventory from the shared provider setup/source inventory contract instead of local `_documentColumns`, `_documentCacheColumns`, or `_heartbeatColumns` arrays.
The expected SQL Server capture-instance column order is derived from the same source inventory consumed by provider setup and connector-template generation.
A DMS core table column change cannot require separate edits in `MssqlCdcSourcePositionAdapter` to keep CDC provider-history validation aligned.
Live inspection remains fail-closed: missing, extra, reordered, or mismatched captured columns still produce provider artifact continuity diagnostics rather than adapting to the live database.
Focused SQL Server source-position adapter tests cover a column inventory generated from the shared source inventory contract and a mismatched live capture-column case.

description: Medium: Make local CDC binding state writes and cleanup deletion ordering fail closed after partial filesystem mutations.
acceptance-criteria: If owner-only permission application fails after a new binding file is created, the local state store deletes the incomplete binding file before returning failure, matching incident latch cleanup behavior.

A failed binding permission application cannot leave an exact-match binding file that a later create or read operation accepts without validated owner-only permissions on platforms where those permissions are supported.
Delete-after-verified-cleanup removes any terminal incident state before deleting the binding record, so the binding record is the last local state file removed for a generation.
Deletion failures report the path and operation that actually failed, distinguishing binding deletion from incident deletion.
Focused local state-store tests use injected permission failures and incident cleanup failures to verify no orphaned or insecure state is accepted.

description: Medium: Validate the complete CDC binding contract before creating or accepting local binding state.
acceptance-criteria: Create-binding and import paths reject invalid `CdcBinding` input before writing any local state file, including wrong `version`, wrong `contractVersion`, unsafe identity fields, nonpositive partition count, unsupported partitioner algorithm, invalid physical-source fingerprint, and non-deterministic connector or topic names.
Read, exact-match, and list operations treat persisted binding JSON as invalid local state when the parsed binding fails the same complete binding validation, even if the file path identity matches.
Complete binding validation verifies deterministic artifact recovery from `topicName` and `connectorName`, not only JSON deserialization and path identity.
Invalid persisted binding diagnostics remain typed and sanitized and are reported as state-store failures rather than valid binding mismatches.
Focused local state-store tests cover attempted creation with invalid binding input and persisted binding files whose path identity matches but immutable binding fields are invalid.

description: Low: Reject duplicate JSON properties recursively when reading local CDC incident state.
acceptance-criteria: Local persisted incident reads reject duplicate JSON properties anywhere in the incident document, including nested `bindingIdentity`, nested `positionMetadata`, and arrays or objects beneath those fields.
Duplicate-property failures are reported as invalid persisted incident state with typed `malformedPayload` diagnostics and are mapped to local state-store failure behavior.
Incident deserialization no longer relies on `System.Text.Json` last-writer-wins behavior after only root properties have been checked.
Binding-file duplicate-property behavior remains fail-closed and is covered by the same recursive duplicate-property helper or an equivalent full-document check.
Focused local state-store tests cover duplicate nested incident fields whose last JSON value would otherwise deserialize to a valid incident.

description: High: Reject or redact sensitive text in CDC opaque evidence fields before it can be serialized as proof or observation evidence.
acceptance-criteria: Shared CDC evidence text handling detects credential, connection-string, Kafka security, source-identity, and database/server/catalog-sensitive fragments before and after whitelist sanitization.

Adoption proof `evidenceSummary`, cleanup proof `evidenceSummary`, initial eligibility `providerConsistencyToken`, and other validated sanitized-evidence fields cannot accept sanitized-but-still-sensitive values such as `database.password=...`, `pwd=...`, `server=...`, `sourceIdentity=...`, or Kafka security settings.
Constructing or deserializing proof and observation DTOs with sensitive evidence text does not preserve those sensitive fragments in serialized CDC contracts, diagnostics, logs, or metrics.
Validators return `unsafeEvidence` diagnostics for rejected sensitive evidence without including the raw sensitive input in diagnostic fields.
Focused proof, observation, and diagnostic privacy tests cover sensitive-fragment inputs with punctuation removed by the whitelist as well as ordinary safe bounded evidence text.

description: High: Require the source-history continuity observation to be ordered between provider-barrier success and the second caught-up projection before initial admission.
acceptance-criteria: Initial admission reports `unknown` with primary blocking category `statusObservationUnavailable` when a healthy source-history observation was captured before the provider barrier reached the committed source offset.

Initial admission reports `unknown` with primary blocking category `statusObservationUnavailable` when the second caught-up projection observation is not after the healthy source-history observation used for admission.

Ordering diagnostics identify the source-history observation path and use `invalidOrdering` without weakening existing source-mismatch, provider-barrier-not-reached, or source-history-lost classifications.

The admission evaluator still admits when same-operation evidence is ordered as first projection caught up, provider barrier reached, source-history continuity healthy, second projection caught up, and lag acceptable.
Focused admission tests cover stale source-history, source-history captured after the second projection, and the valid ordered sequence.

description: Medium: Validate owner-only permissions before accepting local CDC incident state files.
acceptance-criteria: Reading a latched incident for a binding validates that the incident JSON file has owner-only permissions on platforms where owner-only permissions are supported, matching binding-file read behavior.
Deployment-key listing validates owner-only permissions for every incident file before parsing it and fails the whole list operation when an incident file is not owner-only.
Incident files with group/world readable or writable permissions are reported as local state-store failures instead of valid absent, valid latched, or valid binding-present state.
Unsupported-platform permission behavior remains unchanged and continues to allow reads when the permission provider reports unsupported.
Focused local state-store tests cover direct incident read and deployment listing with existing incident files whose owner-only permission validation fails.

description: Medium: Reject a missing CDC target tenant key instead of mapping null to the default binding tenant.
acceptance-criteria: Target input validation maps only the explicit E18 default tenant key empty string to binding tenant key `default`.
A null `CdcTargetInput.TenantKey` is treated as a missing required field at `$.tenantKey` and does not produce a validated target.
Non-default tenant keys continue to pass through unchanged after Kafka-safe token validation.
Binding DTO validation remains aligned with target validation and does not accept null persisted `tenantKey` values.
Focused target-validation tests cover empty-string default mapping, null tenant rejection, and non-default tenant preservation.

description: Medium: Classify invalid SQL Server schema-history enablement phases as unknown instead of emitting invalid source-history observations.
acceptance-criteria: The source-history continuity classifier returns `unknown` with sanitized invalid-enum diagnostics when SQL Server schema-history evidence has an unsupported `enablementPhase` value.
Invalid `enablementPhase` input never falls through to a healthy observation, a terminal lost observation, or an incident candidate carrying the unsupported enum value.
Invalid SQL Server schema-history `state` handling remains fail-closed and continues to return unknown with schema-history unavailable facts.
Valid `beforeInitialAdmission` schema-history problems remain non-latching readiness/setup failures, and valid `afterInitialAdmission` terminal states still create the correct incident candidates.
Focused source-history classifier tests cover invalid enablement phase with `Valid` state and with terminal schema-history states.

description: High: Align the SQL Server Connect source-partition hash encoder with the DMS-1319 conformance vector for quoted and escaped catalog names.
acceptance-criteria: `CdcSourcePartitionHashCalculator.ComputeSqlServer("edfi.dms", "EdFi \"DMS\"\\CDC")` returns `sha256:d4391b11394929abaabadbf53d9a8c3a9c420f91302573966ceeaf12b591fa2a` as specified by the story vector.
The PostgreSQL `edfi.dms` vector and the simple SQL Server `EdFi_DMS_CDC` vector remain unchanged.

The canonical source-partition JSON encoder preserves the design property order and uses one explicit `System.Text.Json` encoder policy so future escaping changes cannot silently drift from the pinned vectors.
The raw SQL Server catalog name remains used only as the hash input and is not emitted in CDC observations, diagnostics, incidents, logs, or metrics.
Connector-offset and source-history code continue to consume the shared source-partition hash calculator instead of duplicating vector constants or JSON encoding logic.

description: Medium: Keep provider-history availability out of the providerSetup component because sourceHistory owns provider-history unknown and lost classifications.
acceptance-criteria: Provider-setup validation and status evaluation no longer make `providerSetup` invalid or unknown solely because `providerHistoryState` is unknown, missing, or mismatched while artifact, grant, source, and heartbeat setup states are satisfied.

Otherwise satisfied provider setup remains `satisfied` when provider-history evidence is unavailable, and the source-history component reports `unknown` with `providerHistoryUnknown` for that same condition.

Provider-history loss evidence, missing recreated provider artifacts, retained-range gaps, and SQL Server schema-history loss continue to flow through the source-history classifier and incident latch rather than the provider-setup component.
Initial admission and regular status evaluation do not report simultaneous providerSetup unavailable or invalid blockers when the only failing evidence is provider-history availability.
Focused validator and evaluator tests cover satisfied setup with unknown provider history, missing provider history, and actual setup inventory mismatches.

description: Low: Report unresolved physical source fingerprints as unavailable evidence instead of sourceMismatch in initial-enable retry diagnostics.
acceptance-criteria: Pre-binding eligibility and exact-binding retry evaluation add an unavailable-evidence diagnostic, not `sourceMismatch`, when the current `physicalSourceFingerprint` is null or blank.
The retry classification, action, and primary blocking category remain fail-closed and continue to use `statusObservationUnavailable` where they do today for unresolved source identity.
Actual source fingerprint mismatches detected by CDC observation validation continue to use the more specific `sourceMismatch` category.
Operator-facing retry diagnostics distinguish an unknown source from a known-but-different source without leaking provider connection, server, database, or credential text.
Focused retry classifier tests cover null and blank fingerprints for both pre-binding and exact-binding retry paths.

description: High: Make local binding retirement fail closed when incident or binding deletion is interrupted.
acceptance-criteria: Delete-after-verified-cleanup persists an owner-only retirement marker for the complete binding identity before deleting terminal incident state.
Retirement deletes incident state before the binding record and deletes the binding record last, preserving the design-owned cleanup order.
While a retirement marker exists, create, read, exact-match, list, latch, and import operations cannot expose or accept the generation as a live binding with a clear incident latch.

A retry with the same valid cleanup proof resumes the marked retirement, completes any remaining idempotent deletions, and removes the retirement marker; mismatched identity or proof input is rejected without mutation.

Injected failure tests cover interruption before incident deletion, after incident deletion, during binding deletion, and during marker removal, and no case leaves an operable binding whose terminal latch was cleared by a partial retirement.

description: High: Observe SQL Server CDC job health and distinguish missing jobs from stopped, failed, or unavailable job state.
acceptance-criteria: The SQL Server source-history adapter records structured capture and cleanup job evidence instead of reducing `sp_cdc_help_jobs` output to one presence boolean.
A successful provider query proving that the binding-required capture or cleanup job is missing returns terminal `providerArtifactMissing` continuity loss and an incident candidate.

A stopped or failed capture or cleanup job returns continuity `unknown`, blocks readiness, and does not create an incident candidate while the exact capture artifacts and retained LSN range still cover the committed offset.
An unavailable or unauthorized job-health query returns continuity `unknown` with sanitized diagnostics and is not misclassified as authoritative job absence.
Healthy continuity requires both required jobs, healthy job state, exact capture instances, and a retained range covering the committed offset.
Focused classifier and SQL Server adapter tests cover healthy, missing, stopped or failed, and query-unavailable job observations.

description: High: Add a usable opt-in controller boundary for CDC state and provider adapters and remove deployment-owned services from default DMS runtime registration.
acceptance-criteria: A production consumer outside the Core and provider backend assemblies can access the required binding lifecycle, barrier capture, and source-history operations through minimal public interfaces without `InternalsVisibleTo`.
The public controller boundary returns stable public CDC contracts and does not expose the current internal state-store result hierarchy or concrete provider adapter classes.

`AddDmsDefaultConfiguration` no longer registers the deployment-owned CDC state store, and ordinary PostgreSQL and SQL Server reference-resolver registration no longer adds otherwise-unused CDC provider adapters.

Explicit opt-in service registration composes the local state store and the selected provider adapter for the 19-04 controller host without adding a DMS HTTP endpoint or binding persistence to the DMS database.

A consumer-level registration test resolves and invokes the public boundary from an assembly that has no internal visibility, while default DMS registration tests prove the deployment controller services are absent.

description: High: Restore default System.Text.Json escaping for canonical Connect source-partition hashes.
acceptance-criteria: Source-partition canonical JSON uses default `Utf8JsonWriter` string escaping and does not configure `JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping` or another custom encoder.
PostgreSQL and SQL Server hashes continue to use one shared canonical encoder with the contract-defined property order and NUL-delimited hash payload.
A pinned SQL Server catalog-name vector containing `<`, `>`, or `&` asserts the hash produced from default-escaped canonical JSON and fails under relaxed escaping.
The existing PostgreSQL, simple SQL Server, and quote/backslash conformance vectors remain covered.
The raw SQL Server catalog name remains an in-memory hash input only and is not emitted through observations, incidents, diagnostics, logs, or metrics.

description: Medium: Timestamp PostgreSQL provider barriers when the WAL boundary is actually captured.
acceptance-criteria: A successful PostgreSQL barrier result records `BarrierCapturedAt` immediately after the `pg_current_wal_lsn()` query completes and the returned LSN is accepted, not before connection opening or query execution.
The success timestamp cannot predate a projection caught-up observation that occurs after barrier capture starts but before the WAL query returns.
Validation and provider-query failures continue to carry a current failure observation time without reporting a successful barrier.
Focused adapter and admission-ordering tests cover a first projection observation between method entry and WAL query completion.

description: Medium: Remove misplaced and duplicated normative CDC text and the source-scanning evidence meta-test from the DMS-1319 work package.
acceptance-criteria: The DMS-1319 story contains only design links, outcome, dependencies, implementation scope, acceptance evidence, and exclusions, and does not repeat algorithms, message fields, fixed values, readiness conditions, or recovery rules owned by the CDC design documents.

The source-partition hash canonicalization rule and conformance vectors needed for 19-04 interoperability are recorded once in the authoritative CDC integration design before being removed from the story.
Acceptance evidence links to the authoritative design owners and names the behavioral test suites without copying design contracts or individual test method names into a second source of truth.
`CdcStoryEvidenceTraceabilityTests.cs`, which only scans test source files for hard-coded names, is removed.
Focused behavioral unit, provider integration, and API integration tests remain the executable evidence for the story.
No production behavior or sibling-story implementation is changed as part of this scope cleanup.

description: High: Order source-history and second-projection evidence after the completed provider-barrier comparison, not merely after the connector offset was read.
acceptance-criteria: A reached provider barrier establishes its success boundary from `CdcProviderBarrierObservation.ObservedAt`, after the captured provider position and connector offset have been compared.
Healthy source-history evidence is accepted for initial admission only when its `ObservedAt` is strictly after the provider-barrier success boundary.
The second caught-up projection is accepted only when its `ProjectionObservedAt` is strictly after the provider-barrier success boundary and after the healthy source-history observation.

Source-history or second-projection evidence observed after `ConnectorOffsetObservedAt` but at or before the provider-barrier observation time makes admission `unknown` with an `invalidOrdering` diagnostic.
Focused admission tests pin the valid sequence and both between-offset-and-barrier-result failure cases.

description: High: Fail closed when current local state-store diagnostics accompany a previously read binding state.
acceptance-criteria: Any current state-store diagnostic makes the binding component `unknown` with primary blocking category `statusObservationUnavailable`, even when `BindingState` is non-null.
A previously read binding or incident is not treated as current authoritative state after the state store reports an unavailable, malformed, or partial read.
The target cannot evaluate to `ready` while state-store diagnostics are present.
The original sanitized state-store diagnostics remain in the target status without adding a misleading binding identity mismatch.
Focused status and admission tests cover a valid binding state combined with current state-store unavailability.

description: High: Consume E19-S01 validate-only provider metadata for source-history classification and remove DMS-1319's duplicate provider-catalog inspection paths.
acceptance-criteria: Source-history classification consumes one normalized mapping of the live `CdcProviderSetupResult` artifact inventory, source-table inventory, provider-history observations, and continuity diagnostics produced by E19-S01 `ValidateOnly`.

The PostgreSQL and SQL Server source-position adapters retain only provider-barrier capture and comparison behavior and do not re-query publication, replication-slot, database CDC, capture-instance, captured-column, retained-range, or SQL Agent job metadata.
An enabled SQL Server capture job reported as not running by E19-S01 maps to `stopped` and continuity `unknown`; it is never mapped to `healthy` because its prior run succeeded or has no history.

A scheduled, enabled, non-running cleanup job remains healthy only when its last completed run succeeded, while disabled, failed, missing, and unavailable states preserve the design's existing continuity classifications.
Backend-specific request/result records and conversion overloads that duplicate the public Core provider-position contracts are removed, and provider tests use the public contracts directly.

The SQL Server backend no longer references the DDL assembly solely to reconstruct the emitted CDC source inventory, and the public `EmitRequiredSourceInventory` helper is removed if it has no remaining caller outside `CoreDdlEmitter`.

Focused mapping, classifier, and provider-position tests cover both providers, retained-range comparison, exact artifact matching, SQL Server job states, and sanitized diagnostics without maintaining a second catalog-query test suite.

description: High: Classify a Connect source-partition hash mismatch as terminal source-history loss instead of returning an unknown observation before the loss classifier runs.
acceptance-criteria: When a successful Connect offset observation carries a source-partition hash different from the binding-derived expected hash, continuity is `lost` with failure category `connectSourcePartitionMismatch`.
The classifier returns a valid incident candidate containing only the expected sanitized source-partition hash and never exposes the raw source-partition JSON or catalog name.
Envelope failures that do not prove a source-partition mismatch remain `unknown` and do not create an incident candidate.
Focused PostgreSQL and SQL Server tests use an exact-match offset result with a mismatched observed hash and prove the terminal classification independently of the source-partition match-result enum.

description: High: Preserve the durable source-history incident latch when local binding retirement is interrupted after one state file is deleted.
acceptance-criteria: Retirement never leaves a readable binding without its previously latched source-history incident after a partial delete failure.
The binding authority is removed before the incident file so an interrupted operation leaves either the complete original state or a fail-closed orphan incident, never an unlatchable binding.
Retrying with the same structurally valid cleanup proof removes an exact orphan incident and completes retirement without requiring the deleted binding file to be reconstructed.
Single-binding reads, deployment listing, and lifecycle results remain not-ready or unavailable throughout every injected delete-failure boundary.
Focused filesystem-failure tests cover failure before binding deletion, failure after binding deletion, and successful retry from the orphan-incident state.

description: Medium: Make CDC diagnostics deterministic and keep internal JSON paths out of the operator-facing `observed` evidence field.
acceptance-criteria: Pure status, admission, retry, validation, and continuity operations produce identical diagnostic timestamps for identical inputs and do not read `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` while constructing diagnostics.
Every generated diagnostic receives an explicit operation or observation timestamp from its evaluation context or injected `TimeProvider`.
The internal `Path` remains available for validation composition and remains excluded from JSON, while `Observed` is null unless the caller supplied an actual sanitized observed value.
`WithPath` changes only the internal path and preserves the diagnostic's existing expected and observed evidence.
The public provider-history mapping path requires an explicit observation timestamp; the redundant overload that timestamps diagnostics with the wall clock is removed.
Focused serialization and evaluator tests assert stable timestamps and prove that validation paths are not serialized as observed evidence.

description: Low: Remove the unused provider-history state from the provider-setup observation now that source-history evidence and status own that classification.
acceptance-criteria: `CdcProviderSetupObservation` no longer contains `ProviderHistoryState`, and its validator handles only provider setup artifacts, grants, source inventory, and heartbeat state.
`CdcProviderSourceHistoryEvidence` and `CdcSourceHistoryObservation` remain the single normalized path for provider-history availability, retained-range, job, and continuity state.
The provider setup mapper does not compute or copy a second provider-history state into the setup observation.
Status and admission tests no longer vary an ignored provider-setup field to prove source-history independence.
The serialized provider-setup contract has no dead provider-history member.

description: Medium: Remove the provider-specific barrier request, result, and observation wrappers that duplicate the shared Core source-position adapter contracts.
acceptance-criteria: The PostgreSQL and SQL Server adapters implement `ICdcProviderSourcePositionAdapter` directly with `CdcProviderBarrierCaptureRequest`, `CdcProviderBarrierCaptureResult`, and `CdcProviderBarrierObservationRequest`.
Provider-specific barrier request, result, and observation record types and their conversion methods are removed.
Each provider has one capture path and one comparison path, with no shared-to-provider-to-shared contract round trip.
Provider integration tests exercise the same public Core contracts consumed by the 19-04 controller.
Provider-specific SQL and position normalization behavior remains unchanged.

description: Low: Revert the unrelated private `CoreDdlEmitter` refactor from the DMS-1319 branch.
acceptance-criteria: `CoreDdlEmitter` retains its pre-branch private source-inventory helper structure and exception behavior.
No DDL output, CDC inventory contract, or provider setup behavior changes as part of this task.
The DMS-1319 diff contains no production DDL-emitter edits that are unrelated to binding, readiness, or the provider-position integration boundary.

description: High: Fail closed when provider-barrier composition receives invalid binding, capture, or connector-offset evidence instead of converting the failure into an ordinary `notReached` barrier for the caller-supplied binding.
acceptance-criteria: PostgreSQL and SQL Server barrier comparison runs only after binding, capture-provider, connector-offset envelope, binding-derived name, and expected source-partition validations succeed.
An operation, target, provider, physical-source, connector-name, topic-prefix, or source-partition validation failure produces an `unknown` barrier and never produces `reached` or `notReached`.
Target status preserves a confirmed source or provider mismatch from barrier input as `sourceMismatch`; other invalid or unavailable barrier input maps to `unknown/statusObservationUnavailable`.
The returned observation does not replace mismatched connector evidence with binding values in a way that makes downstream validation succeed.
Focused tests cover mismatched operation, source fingerprint, connector name, topic prefix, capture provider, and source-partition hash for both provider adapters.

description: High: Correlate each mapped E19-S01 provider setup result to the requested binding instead of synthesizing a satisfied observation from the binding while ignoring the result's provider, mode, outcome, and source fingerprints.
acceptance-criteria: `MapValidateOnlyResult` accepts a successful validate-only result only when `Mode` is `ValidateOnly`, `Outcome` is `ExactMatch`, and the result provider matches the binding provider.
The result's bound physical-source fingerprint and observed physical-source fingerprint are both validated and must exactly match the binding fingerprint before provider setup can be `satisfied`.

A missing observed fingerprint or unavailable validate-only result maps to unknown evidence, while a well-formed different provider or source fingerprint remains an explicit mismatch and cannot be hidden by binding-derived envelope values.
Provider setup and provider-history mapping use the same correlation result so one half of the mapping cannot be satisfied when the other half belongs to another binding.
Focused mapper tests cover wrong mode, failed outcome, wrong provider, wrong bound fingerprint, missing observed fingerprint, and wrong observed fingerprint.

description: High: Preserve known terminal provider-history evidence when an E19-S01 result also contains unavailable observations instead of allowing unavailability to mask a missing, recreated, or lost provider artifact.
acceptance-criteria: A known missing PostgreSQL slot or publication maps to `missing` even when another provider-history query is unavailable.
A known mismatched PostgreSQL slot or publication maps to `recreated`, and explicit WAL loss maps to a retained-history gap, even when other history diagnostics are unavailable.
A known missing or mismatched SQL Server capture instance or missing required CDC job outranks unavailable database-history or retained-range evidence.
Stopped, failed, or unknown SQL Server jobs remain non-terminal unknown readiness when retained history is still proved; they do not create a loss incident.
Mixed-evidence tests prove that every known terminal fact produces `lost` plus an incident candidate and is never downgraded to `unknown`.

description: High: Make a valid durable source-history incident latch authoritative before evaluating fresh diagnostics, expected source-partition hash input, or current provider and connector observations.
acceptance-criteria: A valid incident matching the complete binding identity always produces `lost` with `incidentLatched: true` and no new incident candidate.

Current adapter diagnostics, unavailable provider evidence, malformed current offsets, and an invalid or missing expected source-partition hash cannot downgrade a valid latch to `unknown` or `healthy`.
A malformed, future-dated, or binding-mismatched incident remains fail-closed as unknown and is not reported as a valid latch.
The classifier does not require artifact or source-partition reconstruction to restate position metadata already validated in a matching durable incident.
Focused tests cover a valid latch combined with current diagnostics, invalid expected hash, missing provider setup, and malformed connector offset.

description: High: Distinguish unavailable physical-source evidence from a confirmed physical-source mismatch in the shared observation envelope validator.
acceptance-criteria: A missing physical-source fingerprint when the current source is known produces a missing or unavailable diagnostic but does not also produce `sourceMismatch`.
A malformed physical-source fingerprint produces malformed observation diagnostics but does not produce `sourceMismatch`.
`sourceMismatch` is emitted only when the observation supplies a well-formed fingerprint that differs from the expected fingerprint.
Status and admission map missing or malformed source evidence to `unknown/statusObservationUnavailable` and retain `notReady/sourceMismatch` for a confirmed different fingerprint.
The behavior is covered once at the shared envelope boundary and by focused status and admission assertions.

description: High: Reject symlinks and other invalid filesystem entries in every existing ancestor of a local CDC state path before reporting missing state or reading, writing, listing, or deleting state files.
acceptance-criteria: The configured root and each existing `bindings` or `incidents`, deployment, and instance directory are validated as real directories and not symlinks or reparse points before file existence checks or file I/O.
A symlinked root or intermediate directory returns local state-store unavailability even when the requested generation file is absent.
Read, create, incident latch, list, exact-match, import, and cleanup operations cannot traverse a symlinked ancestor.
Leaf-file symlink rejection and owner-only permission behavior remain intact.
Focused tests cover symlinked root, state-kind directory, deployment directory, and instance directory for both present and missing generation files.

description: Low: Revert the unrelated DMS projection target-initialization behavior change from the DMS-1319 branch.
acceptance-criteria: `Given_DocumentCache_Target_Resolution_Composition` retains the pre-branch failed-initialization expectation and refresh reasons.
DMS-1319 does not change or re-specify same-signature retry behavior owned by the E18 projection target lifecycle.
The branch diff for the target-resolution composition test is empty after the revert.
CDC-specific API-routing evidence in `Given_DocumentCacheStatusEndpointProductionService` remains unchanged.

description: Low: Remove the unused SQL Server heartbeat-sequence materialization and make the fixed heartbeat after-image event serial number a single Core invariant.
acceptance-criteria: The SQL Server heartbeat-after-image query filters on `HeartbeatSequence` but does not select, read, store, or expose that value after the matching row is found.
`SqlServerHeartbeatAfterImage` contains only the start LSN and sequence-value bytes used by barrier capture.
The fixed event serial number `2` is defined once with the Core heartbeat-after-image position contract and is used by capture-result creation and comparison.
`CdcProviderBarrierCaptureResult.SqlServerSuccess` cannot accept a caller-supplied event serial number that differs from the fixed contract.
SQL Server barrier tests continue to assert event serial number `2` in the normalized observation.

description: High: Require SQL Server source-history and provider-barrier evaluation to have the expected Connect source-partition hash before comparing connector offsets.
acceptance-criteria: SQL Server `ObserveProviderBarrier` returns an unknown barrier with a sanitized diagnostic when `ExpectedConnectSourcePartitionHash` is missing.
SQL Server `ObserveSourceHistoryAsync` returns unknown source-history continuity with a sanitized diagnostic when `ExpectedConnectSourcePartitionHash` is missing.
The continuity classifier treats a missing expected SQL Server source-partition hash as unavailable evidence and never reports `healthy` or `lost` from source-partition comparison without it.
PostgreSQL behavior is unchanged: the expected source-partition hash is still derived from the binding-derived topic prefix when omitted.
Focused coverage proves a SQL Server connector offset with an omitted expected hash cannot be accepted as reached or healthy.

description: High: Make provider setup result mapping fail closed when required binding-derived provider artifact or source-history observations are absent.
acceptance-criteria: PostgreSQL mapping reports `ExactMatch` only after finding matched observations for both the expected logical replication slot and publication.
An absent PostgreSQL slot or publication observation maps to `Unknown` with diagnostics unless the provider result explicitly reports `Missing` or `Mismatched`.
SQL Server mapping reports `ExactMatch` only after finding matched observations for every binding-derived capture instance required by the heartbeat, key-change, and document-change artifacts.
SQL Server retained-range mapping requires retained-range history for every required capture instance before reporting `CoversCommittedOffset`.
Empty required grant, heartbeat, or source inventory evidence maps to `Unknown` with sanitized diagnostics and is never mapped as `Matched`.

Focused tests cover absent PostgreSQL slot and publication observations, a missing SQL Server capture artifact observation, a missing SQL Server retained-range history observation, and empty required provider inventories.

description: Medium: Keep the connector-template Backend.Cdc assembly out of DMS-1319 Core observation mapping by removing its new Core project dependency.
acceptance-criteria: `src/dms/backend/EdFi.DataManagementService.Backend.Cdc/EdFi.DataManagementService.Backend.Cdc.csproj` no longer references `EdFi.DataManagementService.Core` solely for CDC status observation mapping.

`CdcProviderSetupResultMapper` and its focused tests are moved out of Backend.Cdc to the smallest existing DMS-1319 integration surface that already needs both provider setup results and Core observation contracts.
`CdcConnectorTemplateIntegrationBoundaryTests` again enforces that the connector-template Backend.Cdc project does not depend on Core.
Backend.Cdc package-lock churn caused by the Core reference is removed.
The move does not add provider provisioning, connector rendering, Kafka mutation, or Kafka Connect mutation behavior.

description: High: Restore same-generation retry for recoverable DocumentCache target initialization failures.
acceptance-criteria: `DocumentCacheTargetRegistry` retries a recoverable provider-prerequisite initialization failure on a supervisor-triggered refresh when the target signature and provider metadata status are unchanged.
A successful retry reuses the existing context generation, creates the execution context, and does not emit `TargetReplaced`.
One non-duplicated recoverable-initialization-failure path drives both the tenant refresh choice and the same-generation rebuild.
Unsupported prerequisite incidents remain non-retryable.
Focused coverage proves the transient provider-prerequisite failure path builds generation `1` twice and becomes eligible after the failure clears.

description: Medium: Make the Core CDC binding and artifact-name contracts the single source consumed by connector-template code.
acceptance-criteria: `Backend.Cdc` connector-template request and result models consume a Core-derived binding/artifact inventory instead of `Backend.Ddl.CdcBindingIdentity`.
`Backend.Ddl.CdcBindingIdentity`, `CdcBindingTopicNames`, and parallel partitioner/topic validation are removed without adding a compatibility shim or independent validation constants.

Connector name, public topic, progress topic, SQL Server schema-history topic, partition count, partitioner algorithm, and provider artifact names all come from the Core binding/artifact-name contract.
Connector-template rendering and validation tests use the single Core binding/name contract.
The cleanup does not add provider provisioning, bootstrap orchestration, Kafka mutation, or Kafka Connect mutation behavior.

description: Medium: Move DDL provider-setup result to Core observation mapping out of test-only code.
acceptance-criteria: `CdcProviderSetupResultMapper` is located in a non-test assembly that can be referenced by E19-S04 production orchestration.
Unit and provider integration tests call the production mapper instead of a `Backend.Tests.Common` implementation.
